answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents post collateral on an escrow wharf to execute tasks. Auditors perform topological cut verifications across transaction graphs to detect collusive clusters. If an unverified subgraph tries to validate a fraudulent sonnet generation, auditors push the cluster over an economic ledge via stake slashing. Corrupting $k$ identities yields superlinear attacker cost $\mathcal{O}(k^2)$ from cross-verifying auditors.
